source: LABBER EN STIL TOT LABBER EN GEMENE BRAMZEILSKOELTE
english: Light and calm to light and moderate topgallant breeze
Double-reefed topsail breeze and courses breeze
Topgallant breeze, topsail breeze and lesser breeze
Topgallant breeze increasing and decreasing by turns
Topgallant breeze diminishing to a faint breeze
Moderate topgallant breeze, light breeze and calm

source: LABBER TOT FRISSE, AFNEMENDE TOT SLAPPE BRAMZEILSKOELTE
english: Light to fresh, decreasing to slack topgallant breeze

source: LABBER EN SLAPPE KOELTE, BRAM EN LEIZEILEN GETOPT
english: Light and slack breeze, topgallant and studding sails topped

source: ZIEN EEN ALBATROS. HEBBEN WEERLICHT EN ONWEDER IN HET NO, DAT EEN VREEMD GELUID GAF, ZOALS KANONSCHOTEN
english: See an albatross. Have lightning and thunder in the NE, which gave a strange sound, like cannon shots

source: ZIEN VLIEGENDE VIS EN EEM PIJLSTRAAT
english: See a flying fish and a tropicbird

source: GEEN KAAPSCHE DUIVEN MEER TE ZIEN.
english: No more Cape pigeons to be seen.
Passing clouds in the forenoon watch
Small clouds drifting over from the NE.

source: KONVOOY MET SLANDS FREGAT BELLONA, SNAUW ZWALUW, BRIK MERCUUR
english: Convoy with the Dutch frigate Bellona, snow Zwaluw, brig Mercuur

source: VLOOT BESTOND UIT DE SCHEPEN: BEHEMOTH, CONCORDIA, OUD HAARLEM, VREEBURG, DOLFIJN
english: Fleet consisted of the ships: Behemoth, Concordia, Oud Haarlem, Vreeburg, Dolfijn
See a ship from the top
A Dutch merchant ship comes in.

source: LIET DE DIEF JAN VAN KERKWIJK NA STELEN VAN PROVIAND STRAFFEN MET 50 SLAGEN, GERRET VENGU EN MICHIEL MEIJER IEDER 20 SLAGEN
english: Had the thief Jan van Kerkwijk punished with 50 lashes for stealing provisions, Gerret Vengu and Michiel Meijer 20 lashes each

source: SOLDAAT CRISTOLF FREDRIK BUHLER VAN STOEKART.
english: Soldier Cristolf Fredrik Buhler of Stuttgart.

source: HADDE VOLGENS GISSING 16 GRADE LENGTE, DUS MAAKT VRIJ WAT VERSCHIL MET DE LANGTE
english: By estimation had 16 degrees of longitude, so makes quite a difference with the longitude

source: DRAAIEN BIJ MET DE ANDERE SCHEPEN. KAPITEIN GAAT MET DE CHALOUP NAAR DE COMMANDANT. ER WORDT BESLOTEN NAAR MAURITIUS TE STEVENEN, OMDAT DE HEER STAVORINUS (KAPITEIN SCHIP GOES?) ZICH NIET IN STAAT ACHTTE OM MET HET BESCHADIGDE TUIG DE REIS NAAR DE KAAP VO
english: Hove to with the other ships. Captain goes with the longboat to the commander. It is decided to put in at Mauritius, because Mr Stavorinus (captain of the ship Goes?) did not consider himself able to make the voyage to the Cape with the damaged rigging ...

source: STOPTE HET GETIJ OM DE WEST.
english: The tide stopped in the west.
At night lightning from SSE - SE

source: WIJ TUIGDEN ONS SCHIP AF EN DANKTEN IN DE NMW ONS VOLK EN GOD ZIJ GELOOFT VOOR EEN BEHOUDEN REIS.
english: We unrigged our ship and in the afternoon watch thanked our people and God be praised for a safe voyage.

source: ZEILENDE VAN SURINAME NAAR ST. EUSTATIUS. BESTEK SINDS 5U30 GEMETEN VAN BRAMSPUNT.
english: Sailing from Suriname to St. Eustatius. Reckoning since 5h30 measured from the topgallant point.

source: KONDEN HET LAND NIET ZIEN DOOR DE DONKERE LUCHT, LATER KLAARDEN HET OP. TEN ANKER OP 16 VOET, MODDER.
english: Could not see the land because of the dark sky, later it cleared. At anchor in 16 feet, mud.

source: 520 TON. GEBOUWD IN 1831 TE KINDERDIJK. VERBOUWD IN 1841 TE KINDERDIJK. 1854 IN VEILING TE ROTTERDAM. IN 1855 GESTRAND EN VERBRIJZELD BIJ SAVANNAH IN DIKKE MIST. DE EQUIPAGE ZOOMEDE EEN KLEIN GEDEELTE DER INVENTARIS IS GEBORGEN.
english: 520 tons. Built in 1831 at Kinderdijk. Rebuilt in 1841 at Kinderdijk. 1854 at auction in Rotterdam. In 1855 stranded and wrecked near Savannah in thick fog. The crew as well as a small part of the inventory were saved.

source: 36 STUKKEN KANON, 10 DRAAIBASSEN, 230 KOPPEN AAN BOORD
english: 36 guns, 10 swivel guns, 230 men on board
V00, V04, V04, clouds rising NNW

source: VISSEN EEN GEBROKEN STENG OP, DIE BLIJKBAAR AL EEN TIJD IN HET WATER LAG.
english: Fished up a broken topmast, which had apparently been in the water for some time.

source: HAALDEN DE ZWARE TOUWEN OP HET DEK
english: Hauled the heavy ropes up on the deck

source: VULDEN ZOUT WATER IN HET RUIM
english: Filling with salt water in the hold

source: ZEE BEGIN ZICHT HET NO TE VEREFFENEN
english: Sea begins to subside in the NE

source: KAPITEIN HARINGMAN EN BISDOM KWAMEN AAN BOORD EN DEELDEN MEE DAT ZIJ DIE DAG EEN RESOLUTIE HADDEN AANGENOMEN DAT EEN OFFICIER MET 30 MAN VAN KAPT. BISDOM EN NOG EEN OFFICIER EN 30 MAN SURINAAMSE EN BERBICIAANSE TROEPEN NAAR ... TE DETACHEREN TENEINDE DE B
english: Captain Haringman and Bisdom came on board and informed us that that day they had adopted a resolution to detach an officer with 30 men of Capt. Bisdom's and another officer and 30 men of Surinam and Berbice troops to ... in order to the b

source: ZIEN EEN BARK, LADEN DE BATTERIJ MET SCHERP
english: See a barque, load the battery with live shot

source: EEN SCHOT MET SCHERP OP EEN ENGELSE SNAUW OM ACHTEROM TE KOMEN.
english: A shot with live shot at an English snow to bring her astern.

source: 'TEGEN DE AVOND DEED DEN VIJAND VAN DE WAL VERSCHEIJDE SCHOOTEN MET SCHERP OP DE SIACSE VAARTUIGEN'
english: 'Towards evening the enemy fired several shots with live shot from the shore at the Siamese vessels'

source: FIRST PART FRESH GALES, MIDDLE AND LATTER HARD GALES AND SQUALLY
english: First part fresh gales, middle and latter hard gales and squally

source: FIRST PART FRESH GALES, LATTER LIGHT AIRS
english: First part fresh gales, latter light airs

source: FIRST AND LATTER PARTS MODERATE BREEZES, MIDDLE SQUALLY
english: First and latter parts moderate breezes, middle squally

source: FIRST PART MODERATE, MIDDLE AND LATTER LITTLE WIND, AT NOON QUITE CALM
english: First part moderate, middle and latter little wind, at noon quite calm

source: FIRST PART LIGHT BREEZE, MIDDLE AND LATTER VARIABLE AIRS AND CALMS
english: First part light breeze, middle and latter variable airs and calms

source: PM MODERATE BREEZES, AM SQUALLY, NOON CALM
english: Pm moderate breezes, am squally, noon calm

source: FIRST AND MIDDLE PART MODERATE, LATTER INCLINABLE TO CALM
english: First and middle part moderate, latter inclinable to calm

source: STRONG BREEZES, 5 MORE MODERATE, AM FINE BREEZES
english: Strong breezes, 5 more moderate, am fine breezes

source: FIRST AND MIDDLE PARTS LIGHT VARIABLE AIRS, LATTER MODERATE BREEZES AND SQUALLY
english: First and middle parts light variable airs, latter moderate breezes and squally

source: FIRST MODERATE, LATTER LIGHT AIRS WITH CALMS
english: First moderate, latter light airs with calms

source: HEAVY SQUALLS, NOON MODERATE BREEZES, 2 MORE MODERATE, SQUALLY, MIDNIGHT STRONG GALES
english: Heavy squalls, noon moderate breezes, 2 more moderate, squally, midnight strong gales

source: FIRST AND MIDDLE PARTS FRESH BREEZES, LATTERLY DECREASING
english: First and middle parts fresh breezes, latterly decreasing

source: PM FIRST PART MODERATE, LATTER FRESH BREEZES AND SQUALLY, AM FRESH BREEZES, NOON MODERATE
english: Pm first part moderate, latter fresh breezes and squally, am fresh breezes, noon moderate

source: FIRST PART FAIR WITH A STEADY GALE, MIDDLE AND LATTER INCLINABLE TO SQUALLS
english: First part fair with a steady gale, middle and latter inclinable to squalls

source: FOUND IN THE SPIRIT ROOM AND COAL ROOM A PIPE OF WINE AND 3 PUNCHEONS OF RUM STORE IN THE HURRICANE.
english: Found in the spirit room and coal room a pipe of wine and 3 puncheons of rum store in the hurricane.

source: FIRST PART CLOUDY, MIDDLE AND LATTER FINE WEATHER
english: First part cloudy, middle and latter fine weather

source: AM CLOUDY NOON FINE 1PM HAZY 6PM FINE 8PM CLOUDY
english: Am cloudy noon fine 1pm hazy 6pm fine 8pm cloudy

source: FIRST PART FAIR, MIDDLE AND LATTER UNSETTLED WEATH
english: First part fair, middle and latter unsettled weath

source: 7 SAIL OF FRENCH MEN OF WAR
english: 7 sail of French men of war

source: AT 5AM HAD ONE MAN MUCH BURNED (STRUCK BY LIGHTNING?)
english: At 5am had one man much burned (struck by lightning?)

source: YEAR WAS 1768, BUT DID NOT COINCIDE WITH THE DAY OF THE WEEK
english: Year was 1768, but did not coincide with the day of the week

source: FIRST AND LATTER PARTS SOME PASSING DRIZZLING RAIN
english: First and latter parts some passing drizzling rain

source: STRONG SWELL FROM THE SW WARD
english: Strong swell from the SW ward

source: CONFUSED SEA AND SWELL FROM WESTWARD
english: Confused sea and swell from westward

source: AU S ET GOUVERNANT AU NE 1/4 E
english: To the S and steering NEbE

source: DEPUIS ONO JUSQUÉ AU NE, PASSANT PAR LE N
english: From WNW to NE, passing by the N

source: VU PLUSIEURS MORCEAUX D'ARBRES, ET DES BALEINES.
english: Saw several pieces of trees, and whales.

source: VU BEAUCOUP D'OISEAUX, ET DU GOEMON.
A PRE MIDI J'AI PARLÉ A UN BATIMENT AMERICAIN
english: In the forenoon I spoke an American vessel

source: PARLÉ Á DIOVENIR DU BRISTOL ET ALLEV A GAMBY
english: Spoke Diovenir of Bristol and Allev of Gamby

source: MARTINIQUE A LA DOMINIQUE, DAINTE LUCIE, SAINT VINCENT, LA GUADALOUPE, LA BARBADE
english: Martinique to Dominica, Dainte Lucie, Saint Vincent, Guadeloupe, Barbados

source: 450 TONS, THREE MASTS, SQUARE RIGGED, COMPLEMENT 113. HET GEDRUKTE BOEK HEET: VOYAGE DE LA PEROUSE AUTOUR DU MONDE. (1797), GEREDIGEERD DOOR M.L.A. MILET-MUREAU. HET BETREFT EEN ZEER BEKENDE REIS WAAROVER OP INTERNET VEEL IS GEPUBLICEERD. HET DERDE DEEL B
english: 450 tons, three masts, square rigged, complement 113. The printed book is called: Voyage de La Perouse autour du monde. (1797), edited by M.L.A. Milet-Mureau. It concerns a very well-known voyage about which much has been published on the internet. The third volume b

source: HET GEDRUKTE BOEK HEET: RELATION DU VOYAGE A LA RECHERCHE DE LA PEROUSE. HET BETREFT EEN ZEER BEKENDE REIS WAAROVER OP INTERNET VEEL IS GEPUBLICEERD. HET TWEEDE DEEL BEVAT EEN TABEL MET METEREOLOGISCHE GEGEVENS, DEZE IS HIER VERWERKT.
english: The printed book is called: Relation du voyage a la recherche de La Perouse. It concerns a very well-known voyage about which much has been published on the internet. The second volume contains a table with meteorological data, this has been processed here.

source: JOURNAL DE CE QUI S'EST PASSE A BORD DU VAISSEAU LE HAARLEMERHOUT DESTINE A CROISER SUR LES VAISSEAUX REVENANT DES INDES ORIENTALES EN L'ANNEE 1753.
english: Journal of what passed on board the ship the Haarlemerhout, destined to cruise for the ships returning from the East Indies in the year 1753.

source: ENTRE EL ENE Y E 1/4 SE
MUY VARIABLE POR EL 1º Y 2º QTE,
english: Very variable through the 1st and 2nd quadrant,

source: PAJAROS CARNEROS Y OTROS PARECIDOS A LOS CHORLITOS COMO CHARRANES DE PLAYA. TAMBIEN SE VIERON BALLENAS.
english: Shearwaters (sheep birds) and others like plovers, such as terns of the beach. Whales were also seen.

source: SE HAN VISTO ABUNDANCIA DE AGUAS MALAS Y TONINAS.
english: Abundance of jellyfish (Portuguese men-of-war) and porpoises were seen.

source: OBSERVA UNA CORRIENTE DE AGUA MUY GRANDE DE COLOR AMARILLO
english: Observes a very large current of yellow-coloured water

source: CARGA DE ORO Y PLATA ACUÑADOS, ORO Y PLATA LABRADOS EN COFRES Y BAULES, ESTAÑO, CACAO, CASCARILLA, ETC.
english: Cargo of coined gold and silver, wrought gold and silver in chests and trunks, tin, cacao, cascarilla, etc.

source: LLEVANDO DINERO DEL REY, DINERO Y JOYAS DE PARTICULARES Y FRUTOS DE LA ZONA: CACAO, COBRE, ESTAÑO, CHOCOLATE, CASCARILLA, AZÚCAR
english: Carrying the king's money, money and jewels of private persons and produce of the region: cacao, copper, tin, chocolate, cascarilla, sugar

source: NAVÍO CARGADO DE CACAO, CASCARILLA, Y 3 MILLONES CON CUATROCIENTOS MIL PESOS PARA EL REY Y PARTICULARES
english: Ship laden with cacao, cascarilla, and 3 million four hundred thousand pesos for the king and private persons

source: CONDUCE 3 MILLONES 363.000 PESOS EN ORO Y PLATA ACUÑADA, 22 CAÑONES DE PLATA LABRADA, UN BAÚL DE ORO LABRADO 62,65 QQ 48 LBS. DE COBRE 230, QQ 33 LBS DE STAÑO 921 ZURRON DE CACAO 144 CAÑONES DE CASCARILLA 80.
english: Carries 3 million 363,000 pesos in coined gold and silver, 22 casks of wrought silver, a trunk of wrought gold 62.65 quintals 48 lbs. of copper 230, quintals 33 lbs of tin 921 sacks of cacao 144 casks of cascarilla 80.

source: SALEN 4 BARCOS: SEPTEMTRION, ASTUTO, SAN LORENZO Y LA FRAGATA LIEBRE, CON CAUDALES DE S. M. Y AL MANDO ESTÁ EL CAPITÁN DE NAVÍO Y MAYOR GENERAL DE LA ARMADA DON ANTONIO DE ARZE.
english: 4 ships sail: Septemtrion, Astuto, San Lorenzo and the frigate Liebre, with the king's treasure, and in command is the captain of the ship and major general of the fleet Don Antonio de Arze.

source: SE AVISTA UN BERGANTIN Y UNA GOLETA
english: A brigantine and a schooner are sighted

source: IBA A RÍO DE JANEIRO. EL NAVÍO FORMA PARTE DE LA ESCUADRA DEL TENIENTE GENERAL MARQUÉS DE CASA TILLY.
english: Was going to Rio de Janeiro. The ship forms part of the squadron of Lieutenant General Marquis of Casa Tilly.

source: A LAS 15:00 MUERE EL SOLDADO DE MARINA DE TABARDILLO
english: At 15:00 the marine soldier dies of typhus

source: A LAS 00:00 MUERE EL SOLDADO DE LA GUARNICION DEL NAVIO JULIAN PONCE DE ASMA "HICE ECHAR AL AGUA SU COLCHÓN, SABANAS Y ALMOHADAS"
english: At 00:00 the soldier of the ship's garrison Julian Ponce de Asma dies "I had his mattress, sheets and pillows thrown into the water"

source: A LAS 16:25 CON CORTA DIFERENCIA MUERE EL SOLDADO DE LA GUARDIA JOSEPH DE MOYA ETICO SEGÚN DICE EL CIRUJANO LACOMBE Y DESPUES DEL AVE MARIA, SIENDO LAS 18:15 SE ECHO AL AGUA EN LA FORMA ACOSTUMBRADA".
english: At 16:25 or thereabouts the soldier of the guard Joseph de Moya dies, consumptive according to the surgeon Lacombe, and after the Ave Maria, at 18:15 he was committed to the water in the customary manner".

source: DESCRIPTORES, VIENTO Y MAR DEL AMANECER, RESTO DEL MEDIODIA
english: Descriptors, wind and sea of the daybreak, remainder of the midday

source: DATOS DEL MEDIODIA O DE LA SINGLADURA
english: Data of the midday or of the day's run

source: CIELOS Y HORIZONTES CON CELAJERIA. LOS DATOS SUELEN SER DEL AMANECER Y LA OBSERVACION DEL MEDIODIA
english: Skies and horizons with scattered clouds. The data are usually from daybreak and the noon observation

source: PARTIDA DE LA HABANA. RUMBO Y DIRECCIÓN DEL VIENTO DEL MEDIODÍA / RESTO DE REFERENCIAS GENERALES
english: Departure from Havana. Course and wind direction at noon / rest of general references

source: FONDEADO. INTENTA HACERSE A LA VELA PERO TIENE QUE REGRESAR POR SER LOS VIENTOS CONTRARIOS
english: Anchored. Tries to set sail but has to return because the winds are contrary

source: DIRIGIÉNDONOS AL PUERTO DE CARTAGENA (...) DIMOS FONDO
english: Steering for the port of Cartagena (...) we anchored

source: ESTE DÍA SE EMPLEÓ LA GENTE EN LA LIMPIEZA
english: This day the people were employed in cleaning

source: (NOTA: DESPUÉS DE ESTE DÍA, HAY UN VOCABULARIO DE LAS ISLAS SANDWICH, TRADUCIDO AL ESPAÑOL, ASÍ COMO LOS REYES DE DICHAS ISLAS)
english: (Note: after this day there is a vocabulary of the Sandwich Islands, translated into Spanish, as well as the kings of those islands)

source: "A LAS 8 DE LA MAÑANA SUSPENDIMOS EL ANCLA (...) Y NOS ACABAMOS DE AMARRAR A LAS 4 DE LA TARDE NO-SE CON DOS ANCLAS" (FIN DEL TRAYECTO ).
english: "At 8 in the morning we weighed the anchor (...) and finished mooring at 4 in the afternoon NO-SE with two anchors" (end of the passage).

source: EXTRACTO DE LAS NOTICIAS HIDROGRÁFICAS CONTENIDAS EN EL 2º VIAJE DEL CAPITÁN T. COOK EN LOS AÑOS 1772 AL 1775 CON LOS BUQUES LA RESOLUCIÓN Y AVENTURA
english: Extract of the hydrographic news contained in the 2nd voyage of Captain T. Cook in the years 1772 to 1775 with the ships the Resolution and Adventure

source: DIARIO DEL 2º PILOTO SALVADOR GUTIÉRREZ DEL NAVÍO ASTUTO (COMANDANTE EL BRIGADIER JOSÉ DE LA SOMAGIA) DEL CALLAO A CÁDIZ
english: Journal of the 2nd pilot Salvador Gutiérrez of the ship Astuto (commander the brigadier José de la Somagia) from Callao to Cádiz

source: DIARIO DE UNA FRAGATA EN COMISIÓN SECRETA QUE SALE DE MONTEVIDEO EN COMPAÑÍA DE LA FRAGATA SOLEDAD Y EL BERGANTÍN SANTIAGO. EL DIARIO SE INTERRUMPE A LOS POCOS DÍAS.
english: Journal of a frigate on secret commission that sails from Montevideo in company with the frigate Soledad and the brigantine Santiago. The journal breaks off after a few days.

source: TURBONADAS CON MUCHO VTO Y AGUA.
english: Squalls with much wind and rain.

source: HORIZ. CON CHUBASCOS, CELAJER. DEL NE
english: Horizons with squalls, scattered clouds from the NE

source: LES CAYÓ 1 RAYO QUE PARTIÓ EL PALO MAYOR Y CAUSÓ MUCHOS DESTROZOS MÁS
english: A lightning bolt struck them, which split the mainmast and caused much more damage

source: LIMPIAN EL CASCO Y EL FORRO DE COBRE
english: They clean the hull and the copper sheathing
With a very confused, tumbling sea

source: MUY FUERTE DEL SE Y ESE
english: Very heavy from the SE and ESE

source: MUY GRANDE Y ENCONTRADA POR TODAS PARTES
english: Very heavy and confused on all sides

source: COMBATES Y ENTREGA DE LA PLAZA POR PARTE DE LOS ENEMIGOS (PORTUGUESES)
english: Combats and surrender of the town by the enemy (Portuguese)

source: EMPIEZA EL APRESTO Y ARREGLO DEL BARCO PARA LA CAMPAÑA DEL N
english: The fitting out and repair of the ship for the campaign of the N begins

source: HORIZONTES AGUACERADOS POR EL 3º Y 4º CUADRANTES
english: Horizons showery in the 3rd and 4th quadrants

source: CIELO Y HORIZONTES CLAROS. ANOCHECIO CIELO CLARO, HORIZONTES CON GRUESA CELAJERÍA
english: Sky and horizons clear. Nightfall clear sky, horizons with thick scattered clouds

source: QUEDAMOS CON LOS HORIZONTES Y CIELOS FOSCOS, EL VIENTO AL OSO BONANCIBLE, CON LA MAR NO GRUESA DEL SO ANOCHECIÓ CON LOS HORIZONTES NOBULOSOS PERO N
english: We remained with the horizons and skies dark, the wind at WSW moderate, with the sea not heavy from the SW. At nightfall the horizons were cloudy but N

source: A LAS 5 1/2 (...) ENTRÓ UNA TURBONADA DEL SE DE VTO, Y GARÚA.
english: At 5 1/2 (...) a squall came on with the wind at SE, and drizzle.

source: AMANEC. HORIZ. Y CIELOS NUBLADOS, MAR LLANA.
english: At daybreak horizons and skies cloudy, sea smooth.

source: VIENTO SE MUI FLOJO VARIO Y CON REPETIDOS CHUBASCOS, A LAS 8 DE LA NOCHE A CAUSA DE QUEDARSE CALMA Y ESTAR TODO EL ORIZONTE SERRADO
english: Wind SE very light and variable and with repeated squalls, at 8 at night owing to its falling calm and the whole horizon being closed in

source: CARGADOS DE NUBES LLUVIAS CON TRUENOS Y RELÁMPAGOS
english: Heavy with clouds, rains with thunder and lightning

source: QUEDAMOS (...) CON CIELO Y HORIZ. CON ALGUNA CELAJ. SUELTA, VTO BONANCIBLE, MAR DEL VTO (...) ANOCHEC. Y AMANECIÓ LO MISMO.
english: We remained (...) with sky and horizon with some scattered clouds, wind moderate, sea from the wind (...) at nightfall and daybreak the same.

source: ANOCHECIÓ CLARO, LOS HORIZ. CON ALGUNA CELAJER., VTO BONANCICBLE Y MAR LLANA. AMANECIÓ EL CIELO CON CELAJER. SUELTA, LOS HORIZ. MÁS CARGADOS, VTO FRES
english: Nightfall clear, the horizons with some scattered clouds, moderate wind and smooth sea. Daybreak the sky with loose scattered clouds, the horizons more heavy with cloud, fresh wind...

source: VIENTO QUE DEMUESTRA..., ANOCHECIÓ CLARO HORIZONTES CALIMOSOS VIENTO BONANCIBLE POR EL MISMO MAR SORDA DEL N..., AMANECIÓ EN LOS M
english: Wind that shows..., at nightfall clear, horizons hazy, wind moderate from the same quarter, dull sea from the N..., at daybreak in the m

source: CIELO NUBLADO Y HORIZ. CARGADO. A LAS 4 (DE LA TARDE) AFLOJÓ UN POCO EL VTO PERO SE PUSO TODO EL CIELO Y HORIZ. OSUCROS, VUE CALMANDO EL VTO Y LLMÁNDO
english: Sky cloudy and horizon heavy with cloud. At 4 (in the afternoon) the wind slackened a little but the whole sky and horizon became dark, the wind went calm and callin

source: CIELOS CLAROS Y HORIZONTES CARGADOS. A LAS 0:00 EMPEZO A TRONAR Y RELAMPAGUEAR POR EL 4º CUADRANTE CON FUERTES AGUACEROS
english: Skies clear and horizons heavy with cloud. At 0:00 it began to thunder and lighten in the 4th quadrant with heavy showers

source: CIELOS Y HORIZONTES OSCUROS Y ATURBONADOS MAYORMENTE POR EL 3º Y 4º CUADRANTES DESPIDIENDO REPETIDOS AGUACEROS
english: Skies and horizons dark and squally, mostly in the 3rd and 4th quadrants, discharging repeated showers

source: A LAS 21:00 SOPLO VIENTO FRESCO DE NO
english: At 21:00 a fresh breeze blew from NW

source: ANOCHECIÓ CON HORIZONTES CARGAOS, L MAR Y EL VTO FUERTE DEL NO.
english: Nightfall with horizons heavy with cloud, the sea and the wind strong from the NW.

source: ANOCHEC. HORIZ. OFUSCADOS, MAR LLANA, VTO CUASI CALMA (...) AMANEC. COMO ANOCHEC., EL VTO DICHO FRESQUITO. POR LA NOCHE HUBO SUS CHUBASQUITOS.
english: At nightfall horizons obscured, sea smooth, wind almost calm (...) at daybreak as at nightfall, the said wind moderate fresh. In the night there were some light squalls.

source: ANOCHEC. HORIZ. CALIMOSOS, VTO CASI CALMA, (...). AMANEC. TOLDADO, HORIZ. CARGADOS, MAR LLANA.
english: Nightfall horizons hazy, wind almost calm, (...). Daybreak overcast, horizons heavy with cloud, smooth sea.
At nightfall with the horizons clear.

source: VIENTO NO FRESCO, LA MAR LLANA. EN LA SINGLADURA ORIZONTES Y CIELO DESPEJADOS.
english: Wind not fresh, the sea smooth. At the day's run horizons and sky clear.
